title: Flocculation Tank

introduction.definition: A flocculation tank stirs coagulated water gently for 15–30 minutes so small particles collide and stick together into large, heavy flocs. This tank has three compartments in series with horizontal paddle reels; each stage turns more slowly than the last (tapered energy) so the growing flocs are not broken.
applications: Ahead of clarifiers and lamella settlers in water treatment
key_points: Tapered energy: G falls stage by stage
introduction.summary: A flocculation tank gently stirs coagulated water so tiny particles collide and stick together into large flocs that settle easily. Horizontal paddle reels in three stages run at decreasing speeds.

pressure.title: Tapered mixing energy
pressure.description: Flocculation needs gentle mixing for 15–30 min. Energy is highest in the first stage (G ≈ 50–70 s⁻¹) to promote collisions and lowest in the last (G ≈ 10–20 s⁻¹) so the large, fragile flocs are not broken up before settling. The product G·t (≈ 10⁴–10⁵) is a key design number.

foundation: Reinforced-concrete tank on prepared ground; watertightness test before backfill; allow for buoyancy when empty (groundwater).
alignment: Weirs and launders levelled to a few millimetres so overflow is even; drive/bridge centred and level.
piping: Inlet arranged to spread flow without short-circuiting; sludge lines with flushing points; overflow and drain to a safe place.
commissioning: Fill with clean water, check for leaks; run mechanisms empty and with water; start chemical dosing and tune by jar tests.

routine.task: Check paddle speeds and floc appearance.

lubrication: Motor and drive bearings greased / oiled to maker schedule; gearbox oil changed by hours or oil analysis.

safety: Guard drives; handrails at open tanks.

video_tutorials.title: Flocculation Tank — Introduction

script.narration: This module introduces the Flocculation Tank.
A flocculation tank stirs coagulated water gently for 15–30 minutes so small particles collide and stick together into large, heavy flocs.
This tank has three compartments in series with horizontal paddle reels; each stage turns more slowly than the last (tapered energy) so the growing flocs are not broken.
Typical applications include ahead of clarifiers and lamella settlers in water treatment; industrial wastewater physico-chemical treatment.
The cutaway reveals the internal construction: Paddle Reel 1 (speed tapers stage by stage), Paddle Reel 2 (speed tapers stage by stage), Paddle Reel 3 (speed tapers stage by stage).
The exploded view separates every component so each one can be tapped for its function, material and failure modes.
Next, watch the operation tutorial to see how it works.

Coagulated water enters stage 1.

Water passes under the first baffle into stage 2.

script.narration: Maintenance essentials for the Flocculation Tank.
Check paddle speeds and floc appearance.
Inspect shaft seals and bearings.
Drain; replace worn paddle boards.
Watch for pin-point floc: small flocs, poor settling. Common cause: under-dosing.
Watch for shaft seal leak: water at drive side. Common cause: seal wear.
Record every inspection so trends — vibration, temperature, leakage and performance — can be compared over time.
